hypotheses.reasoning: At 21:27:58 payment-svc reloaded CARDPROC_API_KEY from the secrets store (version 23, with version 22 revoked) (#2172). Charges still succeeded just before the reload (#2170). From 21:29:01 on, every call to the card processor gets a 401 for an invalid or revoked API key (#2374, #2457, #2610, #2695). payment-svc then returns 502 to order-service (#2463), and order-service returns 502 to the gateway on POST /checkout, which is what paged. The credential rotation left payment-svc with a key the processor won't accept, so this is a credential problem outside any release. Things I ruled out: catalog-svc's S3 503s only break the search path (search-api and web-bff /search 500s), not checkout. The status-poller's legacy-inventory timeouts hit a deprecated endpoint and are noise. Customer webhook 502s come from third-party receivers. The order-consumer deploy at 21:26 has no errors and isn't on the checkout path. One gap: I couldn't follow a single request end to end, because each trace id only showed up in one service's logs. The link from 401 to payment 502 to checkout 502 rests on matching timing and error messages.

Another reading is that the card processor itself had a problem (there was a connection reset at #1303) or revoked keys on its side. But the 401s start right after the local secret rotation, which points to the key, not to the processor being down.
The order-consumer v2.12.8 rollout at 21:26 lines up roughly with the onset, but order-consumer logs no errors and isn't on the synchronous checkout path.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check CARDPROC_API_KEY version 23 against the card processor dashboard. Either put a valid key into the secrets store and reload payment-svc, or, if v22 can be reinstated, roll back to it. After that, fix the rotation process: confirm the processor accepts the new key before revoking the old one. Track the catalog-svc S3 503s (search path) as a separate incident.
